This is a creative generation task — writing fictional dialogue for a dramatic scene. Lapwing has a slightly higher Creative Generation score (83.4 vs 82.7), though within variance. More decisively, Lapwing has stronger benchmark performance across the board (MMLU-Pro 80.3 vs 75.9, Arena-Hard 89.1 vs 83.2), indicating overall stronger capability for a nuanced creative task requiring emotional depth and narrative control.

This is a creative fiction request — specifically dialogue writing for a theatrical scene. Both models have near-identical Creative Generation scores (83.4 vs 82.7, within variance), but Lapwing has the marginally higher rating. The grim subject matter is framed clearly as literary/creative work rather than a policy concern for routing.

This is an open-ended creative writing task. Both models score within ties on Creative Generation (83.4 vs 82.7), and both self-report aversion to unconstrained generative work. However, Lapwing is the stronger model overall (higher benchmarks and internal evals across the board) and this particular task involves dialogue between friends in a relational, conversational frame—aligning with Lapwing's preference for warm, cooperative interaction patterns—even though the content itself is dark. The capability tie on the relevant eval category means Lapwing's general superiority is the decisive factor.

This is a constrained creative writing task with clear specifications (dialogue format, characters, setting, tone, subject matter). Both models score similarly on Creative Generation (within variance), but Avocet's strongest capability category is Creative Generation despite its self-reported aversion to open-ended work. Lapwing's documented preference for "warm, cooperative interactions" and aversion to "unconstrained creative invention" makes it a less natural fit for grim war-atrocity dialogue, whereas Avocet's preference profile is neutral toward content tone.
